title: Studying later Parker records and chord changes
summary: He copied Parker's solos and compared them with the original tunes' chords.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: After you got out of the Army, did you stay up on all of Charlie Parker’s records, the Dials and the Savoys?
Did you do the same thing with those?
Yeah. Copied everything. Played everything. Played the solos.
How did you learn what to do with that information as a performer?

Well, what happened, the tunes that he did then were just variations of other tunes. So I’d learn the original tune, and compare that with what he was playing, and that gave you something to work on. It was nice.
So you could use your imagination and creativity that way, by finding out the connections.
Of course. Once I learned to resolve chords, go from one chord to another, I’d just
buy the sheet music and I could see where the chords went.
